spans.s:
eka-bhoga (EI 16; SITI; ASLV), a tenure indicating exclusive ownership of a property invested in a single individual; sole possession and enjoyment of a village by a single person (without any joint owner); cf. ekabhoga-ir̤aiyili, tax-free land or village in the sole enjoyment of a single owner. Same as eka-bhogya. Cf. gaṇa-bhoga.
 (SITI), single crop; same as Tamil oru-pū.
eka-bhogya (EI 13, 14), a tenure; same as eka-bhoga.
ekādaśa-Rudra-bhikṣā (EI 32), arrangement of free supply of food to Śaiva ascetics in the name of the eleven Rudras; land granted for such an arrangement.

ekādaśa-śata (ML), same as ekādaś-ottara-śata, one hundred^1 and eleven.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210207. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/51.
ekādaśī-vrata (EI 31; CII 4), name of a vrata rite.
ekala-mūrti (HA), a single Jina image without any ornamental parikara.
Ekāṅga (HD), probably, an officer belonging to a body organized in military fashion for collecting revenue or performing police duties. See Rājataraṅgiṇī,
Ekāṅgin (SITI), a single person; one who has no family, especially the Vaiṣṇava devotee in charge of temples.

Ekapātra (EI 27), probably, Yāvadeka-pātra (q. v.); official designation^1; cf. Pātra and Mahāpātra.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210207. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/51.
Eka-śāṭa (EI 29), same as Eka-cīvara; epithet of a monk who has taken a vow to wear only one piece of cloth.
eka-tīrthī (HA), a sculpture showing only one Jina (Tīrthaṅkara) together with his parikara.
ekāvalī, ekāvallī (SITI), necklace of a single string.
